title.value: Bugs in the Data: How ImageNet Misrepresents Biodiversity
title.justification: The title clearly states the main focus of the paper which critiques how ImageNet represents biodiversity in its dataset.
title.quote: Bugs in the Data: How ImageNet Misrepresents Biodiversity

extractions.description: The paper critically examines ImageNet-1k, a dataset used widely for ML benchmarking, with a focus on its representation of wildlife. The authors, collaborating with ecologists, analyze the dataset's 13,450 images of wild animals, finding incorrect labels and significant geographical and cultural biases. The study highlights the problematic nature of the dataset used for training ML models in wildlife-related tasks and calls for improved methods in ML dataset creation and curation.

climate_change_is_central.justification: While the paper addresses biodiversity, which is related to environmental science, it does not explicitly focus on Climate Change.
climate_change_is_central.quote: Our findings highlight serious issues with the extensive use of this dataset for evaluating ML systems, the use of such algorithms in wildlife-related tasks, and more broadly the ways in which ML datasets are commonly created and curated.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper focuses on how the ImageNet dataset misrepresents biodiversity, specifically in its images of wildlife.
primary_sub_category.quote: The ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge (ILSVRC) dataset, commonly called ImageNet-1k, [20] is a subset of the full ImageNet dataset [8] that is used widely in categorical object recognition (with 32k citations to date). More than a quarter of the dataset consists of images of wild animals.
